content: If I have a docs#Filter.HasBasis, then any larger collection containing the same sets should also be one. Is there a direct theorem for this? I'm struggling to even write down this statement.
docs#Filter.HasBasis.to_Basis' can be used to prove this but I don't know if that's quite its intended usage

Indeed that’s one of the downsides of the choice to use families of sets instead of sets of sets (but this downside is compensated by many many upsides imo). Indeed docs#Filter.HasBasis.to_hasBasis and docs#Filter.HasBasis.to_hasBasis' are the most convenient ways to build a basis out of another one, but there are also specific things lower in the same file which may be useful.
Could you give more details about your situation ?

use families instead of using families

I suppose the second "families" should be "sets"? :)

My specific situation is ZeroDimensionalSpace.of_hasBasis in #40901. A zero dimensional space is one where all clopen neighborhoods form a basis for 𝓝 x, so if a (potentially smaller) family of clopen sets also forms a basis, the space must be zero-dimensional. My current proof is six lines, but it really does seem that this should be a one-liner.

Violeta Hernández said:

If I have a docs#Filter.HasBasis, then any larger collection containing the same sets should also be one.

what do you mean "larger collection" containing the "same sets"? is it larger or not? since it contains the same sets doesn't that mean it's the same collection (extensionality)?
won't you also then need the condition that the other sets are all in the filter?
Maybe my six line proof is as good as it gets
